key_evidence_spans: A 10-day-old full-term boy was admitted with viral gastroenteritis
A left hydrocele was diagnosed, and he was discharged
Seventeen days later, at four weeks of age, he returned with a 24-hour history of left scrotal swelling, erythema, fever, and a pus-like discharge from an ulcerated area of the left hemi-scrotum
A provisional diagnosis of missed neonatal testicular torsion was made
Intravenous amoxicillin-clavulanate and flucloxacillin and fluids were started in light of the local scrotal infection
Scrotal examination revealed a left scrotal abscess with a hard, swollen left testis; no hernia was identified
